svg.title: RMR operator panel
svg.text: Sheet 2D: the operator panel from the front at 1:1.75 (plate, window and display as modelled in CAD/Operator Panel; the controls' sizes assumed), and what each control wires to. The dashed outline is the panel as it may grow.
window onto the 10.1 in display, Pi 5 behind it (Touch UI, Jog tab)
push to stop, twist to release
starts the motors after an E-stop
Run All, or resume a hold
To use the screen without touching it (gloves,
dirty hands). Not designed: how the keys reach
the Pi (a USB keypad sends arrows and Enter with
no new wiring; GPIO keys would need new bridge
actions, as S6 and S7 have), and how the Touch
S1, S2, S3, S6, S7: a 22.3 mm hole each; their collars measure 21.8 mm.
Cut one test hole first: 22.3 mm is the usual 22 mm device hole, not read
Plate 5 to 6 mm thick at most, less any legend plate under a collar
(S2's yellow plate): the collar nuts reach no further.
S2's base clamps with two angled screws whose round tips bear on the
plate's back: keep the back flat and bare round its hole.
Screen: VESA 75 x 75 on its back, from the scan of 2026-11-11.
Model (issue #219): CAD/Operator Panel, plate 408 x 228 x 3.17,
window 222.7 x 141.7 onto a 244.7 x 159.7 display; a 2020 ring
behind it, and two spines for a monitor arm (VESA 100).
Pi GPIO 20 and GND, 1 k to 3V3
Sheet 2D (2A, 2B: the decks; 2C: names). Legal 14 x 8.5 in, 100 %.
Status: plate and 2020 frame laid out (#219); the arm not chosen.
